# Math and lists

Numeric helpers. Results are rounded to float32 like MultiCharts. The trigonometric words work in degrees.

[Back to the keyword reference index](README.md)

### AbsValue

| Kind | Returns | Arguments | Argument types | Evidence | On MC compile list | Run status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| builtin | numeric | 1 | numeric | capture (strategy-level) | no | runs |

Absolute value: the number without its sign.

```easylanguage
Vars: Range(0);
Range = AbsValue(Close - Open);
```

### Crosses

| Kind | Returns | Arguments | Argument types | Evidence | On MC compile list | Run status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| builtin | bool | none (used as a value) | not established | capture (strategy-level) | no | runs |

Used in `A crosses above B` or `A crosses below B`: true on the bar where A moves from one side of B to the other. It only works in that phrase.

```easylanguage
Vars: Fast(0), Slow(0);
Fast = Average(Close, 5);
Slow = Average(Close, 20);
If Fast crosses above Slow Then Buy Next Bar At Market;
```

### Random

| builtin | numeric | at least 1 | not established | PowerBridge test (`tests/test_release_020_regressions.py`) | no | transpiles; the run stops (not implemented in the runtime) |

### Round

| Kind | Returns | Arguments | Argument types | Evidence | On MC compile list | Run status |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| builtin | numeric | 2 | numeric, numeric | capture (strategy-level) | no | runs |

Rounds the first argument to the number of decimals given by the second. The result is a float32, so it may print as a close neighbour such as 2.3499999.

```easylanguage
Vars: R(0);
R = Round(Close / 3, 2);
```
